title: Grace, Mercy, and Peace
subtitle: 1–2 Timothy & Titus in Poems & Pictures
author: Timothy Holt
beforeYouBegin:
These are letters from an older man to younger ones. Paul writes to Timothy in Ephesus and to Titus on Crete about elders and households, prayers and meals, widows keeping a lamp lit night and day. Then, from a prison in Rome, he writes once more to Timothy: remember your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, stir up the gift, I have finished the course, and please bring my cloak and the parchments before winter.

This book walks through them in forty short poems, in five parts: two for 1 Timothy, two for 2 Timothy, and one for Titus. Each poem sits beside a picture and under a single line of Scripture. The pictures stay with the things the letters touch—a rolled letter, a banked fire, a clay cup, a folded cloak—and leave the faces to your imagination.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Open the letters to Timothy and Titus alongside this book, and let the real words have the last word.

paintings.title: my true child
paintings.epigraph: “to Timothy, my true child in faith”
paintings.poem:
he could have addressed it
to my assistant.
to my colleague.
to the man I left in charge.

he wrote
my true child.

some families
are made by birth.

some are made
by walking the same roads
long enough
that the older one's faith
starts to show
in the younger one's steps.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Every stop on the Pilgrim Walk shows how God meets us in ordinary places (1 Timothy 1:2)—where in your own home or work today does “some are made by walking the same roads long enough that the older one's faith starts to show in the younger one's steps” ring true?
paintings.zh_poem:
他本可以在信首写：
致我的助手。
致我的同工。
致我留下来主持大局的人。

他却写下：
我的真儿子。

有些家人
是因血缘而生。

有些家人，
则是因同走一条路
走得够久，
以至于年长者的信心
渐渐显在
年轻人的步履之中。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 天路同行的每一站都向我们显明，神如何在平凡之处与我们相遇（提摩太前书 1:2）——今天在你的家中或工作里，哪一处让你深感“有些家人，则是因同走一条路走得够久，以至于年长者的信心渐渐显在年轻人的步履之中”的真实？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “写信给那因信主作我真儿子的提摩太”

paintings.title: the goal
paintings.epigraph: “the goal of this command is love, out of a pure heart and a good conscience and sincere faith”
paintings.poem:
there were men in Ephesus
arguing over family trees
and endless lists of names.

Paul cuts through it
in one line.

the point
was never to win.

the point
is love.

from a clean heart.
a clear conscience.
a faith with nothing to hide.

every rule, every sermon,
every late-night argument
is meant to end up there,

or it has lost the road.10
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Take a slow breath and read the final line again: “every rule, every sermon, every late-night argument is meant to end up there, or it has lost the road.10.” How would you walk through the next hour differently if you carried that truth with you?
paintings.zh_poem:
在以弗所，有些人
正为家谱
和无穷无尽的名字争论不休。

保罗用一句话
切中要害。

目的
从来不是为了争赢。

目的
乃是爱。

出于清洁的心、
无亏的良心、
毫无隐瞒的信心。

每一条规矩、每一篇讲道、
每一次深夜的辩论，
都当归向那里，

否则便是迷了路。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 深吸一口气，再读一遍最后那行诗：“每一条规矩、每一篇讲道、每一次深夜的辩论，都当归向那里，否则便是迷了路。”如果你带着这份真理走入接下来的一个小时，你的脚步会有何不同？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “但命令的总归就是爱；这爱是从清洁的心和无亏的良心，无伪的信心生出来的。”

paintings.title: the worst of them
paintings.epigraph: “Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am chief.”
paintings.poem:
blasphemer.
persecutor.
insolent.

he lists it plainly,
like an old address.

then he writes
the surest sentence he knows:
Christ Jesus came
to save sinners,

of whom I am chief.

not was.
am.

if the first in line
was the worst in line,
then the line
is long enough
for you.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Think of a season when you knew the feeling of “blasphemer. persecutor.” Looking through the lens of 1 Timothy 1:15–16, what does it mean to discover that “if the first in line was the worst in line, then the line is long enough for you”?
paintings.zh_poem:
亵渎神的。
逼迫人的。
侮慢人的。

他坦然列出这一切，
像提起一个旧住址。

随后他写下
他所确知最笃定的一句话：
基督耶稣降世，
为要拯救罪人，

在罪人中我是个罪魁。

不是“曾是”，
而是“正是”。

如果排在队伍最前面的，
是最不堪的那一个，
那么这支队伍
就足够长，
长到容得下你。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 回想一段你曾体会过“亵渎神的。逼迫人的”那种沉重愧疚的时光。透过提摩太前书 1:15–16 的眼光，发现“如果排在队伍最前面的，是最不堪的那一个，那么这支队伍就足够长，长到容得下你”对你意味着什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “基督耶稣降世，为要拯救罪人。在罪人中我是个罪魁。”

paintings.title: shipwreck
paintings.epigraph: “holding faith and a good conscience”
paintings.poem:
Paul knew about ships.
he had seen more than one
go to pieces.

some, he warns,
thrust away a good conscience
and made shipwreck
of their faith.

not a storm
that came for them.
something they threw overboard
because it felt heavy.

hold on to it, Timothy.

it is ballast,
not burden.

it is what keeps you
upright
when the wind turns.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look closely at the quiet centerpiece of “shipwreck” in this painting (1 Timothy 1:18–19)—if you could leave one anxious weight beside it today, what would you set down?
paintings.zh_poem:
保罗熟悉船只。
他不止一次亲眼见过
船只撞得粉碎。

他警戒说，有些人
丢弃良心，
就在真道上
如同船破坏了一般。

不是因为风暴
扑向了他们，
而是他们嫌它沉重，
亲手将它抛进了海里。

提摩太啊，要持守住它。

它是压舱石，
不是累赘。

当风向转变时，
正是它使你
依然平稳直立。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 细看这幅画中《船破坏了》那安静的画面中心（提摩太前书 1:18–19）——如果今天你可以把一件焦虑的重担放在它旁边，你会放下什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “常存信心和无亏的良心”

paintings.title: for everyone
paintings.epigraph: “who desires all people to be saved and come to full knowledge of the truth.”
paintings.poem:
pray for everyone,
he says.
first of all.

for the emperor
who will never know your name.
for the magistrate.
for the neighbor
who knows it too well.

not because they're good.
because God
wants every one of them
saved.

the quiet life
starts here,
at a table,
holding up the names
of people
you would rather
argue with.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Let your eyes rest on the brushwork and light around the stone well in the heat of the day: what quiet prayer rises in you when you read, “the quiet life starts here, at a table, holding up the names of people you would rather argue with”?
paintings.zh_poem:
他说：
第一要为万人恳求。

为那位永远不会知道你名字的
君王。
为官长。
也为那个对你知之甚详的
邻舍。

不是因为他们良善，
而是因为神
愿意他们每一个人
都得救。

平静安稳的生活
从这里开始：
在桌前，
托起那些
你本宁愿与之争辩的
名字。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 让目光停留在画中围绕着安静桌前的笔触与光线：当你读到“平静安稳的生活从这里开始：在桌前，托起那些你本宁愿与之争辩的名字”时，你心中升起怎样安静的祷告？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他愿意万人得救，明白真道。”

paintings.title: one
paintings.epigraph: “For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus”
paintings.poem:
between the holy
and the ordinary.
between God
and someone like me.

there is not
a ladder
of better people.

there is not
a fee.

there is one man
standing in the gap,
the man Christ Jesus,

who gave himself
as a ransom for all.

one.
enough.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Linger with the movement in “one” (1 Timothy 2:5–6) from “between the holy and the ordinary” to “there is one man standing in the gap, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a ransom for all. one. enough”—where do you find yourself along that arc today?
paintings.zh_poem:
在至圣者
与平凡人之间。
在神
与像我这样的人之间。

并没有一架
由更优秀之人组成的阶梯。

也没有一笔
需要缴纳的费用。

只有一人
站在破口之中，
就是降世为人的基督耶稣，

他舍自己
作万人的赎价。

只有一位。
已然足够。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在《只有一位》（提摩太前书 2:5–6）中细细品味那份转折——从“在至圣者与平凡人之间”到“只有一人站在破口之中，就是降世为人的基督耶稣，他舍自己作万人的赎价。只有一位。已然足够”——今天你发现自己处在这段弧线的哪个位置？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “因为只有一位神，在神和人中间，只有一位中保，乃是降世为人的基督耶稣”

paintings.title: a pillar
paintings.epigraph: “the assembly of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.”
paintings.poem:
he hoped to come soon.
he wrote in case
he couldn't.

here is how to live,
he says,
in God's house.

and the house
isn't a building.

it's a few families
in someone's courtyard.
a lamp. a borrowed table.
people who don't agree
on much.

and God calls that
a pillar.

something
the truth
can stand on.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Notice how “a pillar” (1 Timothy 3:14–15) arrives at: “something the truth can stand on.” Who in your life is walking a hard stretch of road today and needs you to share this grace with them?
paintings.zh_poem:
他盼望快到他那里去，
却还是写下这信，
以防耽延。

他说：
这是在神的家里
当怎样行。

而这家
并不是一座建筑。

那是某个人院子里的
几户人家。
一盏灯，一张借来的桌子，
一群在许多事上
意见并不一致的人。

神却称它为
柱石。

是真理
可以稳稳立于其上的地方。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 留意《柱石和根基》（提摩太前书 3:14–15）如何落脚于：“是真理可以稳稳立于其上的地方。”今天在你的生命中，有谁正走在一程艰难的路上，需要你与他们分享这份恩典？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “这家就是永生神的教会，真理的柱石和根基。”

paintings.title: the mystery
paintings.epigraph: “Without controversy, the mystery of godliness is great”
paintings.poem:
it may have been a song
before it was a sentence.

revealed in the flesh.
justified in the spirit.
seen by angels.
preached among the nations.
believed on in the world.
received up in glory.

a mystery,
not because it's hidden,
but because it's
bigger than we are.

and it has
a name.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: What if the most important thing you remember before tonight is the quiet lesson of 1 Timothy 3:16: “a mystery, not because it's hidden, but because it's bigger than we are. and it has a name”?
paintings.zh_poem:
在成为一句话之前，
它或许曾是一首歌。

在肉身显现，
被圣灵称义，
被天使看见，
被传于外邦，
被世人信服，
被接在荣耀里。

称之为奥秘，
不是因为它隐藏不见，
而是因为它
远比我们浩大。

并且这奥秘
有一个名字。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果在今晚入睡前，你最需要记住的是提摩太前书 3:16 那安静的启示：“称之为奥秘，不是因为它隐藏不见，而是因为它远比我们浩大。并且这奥秘有一个名字”——这会带给你怎样的敬畏与安慰？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “大哉，敬虔的奥秘，无人不以为然！”

paintings.title: with thanksgiving
paintings.epigraph: “For every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected, if it is received with thanksgiving.”
paintings.poem:
some teachers
wanted a smaller table.
no this. no that.
holiness by subtraction.

Paul pulls the chairs
back in.

the bread is good.
the figs are good.
the wedding is good.
God made them.

what makes a meal holy
isn't what's missing from it.

it's the word of God,
and a prayer,
and open hands.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Imagine standing inside this frame beside the table set before you: what hurry or noise in your week begins to fade when you hear, “it's the word of God, and a prayer, and open hands”?
paintings.zh_poem:
有些师傅
想要一张更窄小的饭桌：
不可碰这个，不可尝那个——
靠做减法来博取圣洁。

保罗却把椅子
重新拉回桌旁。

饼是好的。
无花果是好的。
婚筵也是好的。
都是神所造的。

使一顿饭成为圣洁的，
不在于桌上少了什么，

而在于神的道、
一句感恩的祷告，
以及摊开的双手。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象自己站在这幅画框里、守在摆设整齐的饭桌旁：当你听见“而在于神的道、一句感恩的祷告，以及摊开的双手”时，你这一周里的哪些匆忙与喧嚣开始渐渐消退？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “凡神所造的物都是好的，若感谢着领受，就没有一样可弃的”

paintings.title: your youth
paintings.epigraph: “Let no man despise your youth; but be an example to those who believe”
paintings.poem:
too young,
someone must have said.

Paul doesn't tell him
to argue.
he doesn't tell him
to wait.

he says:
be the example.

in the way you talk.
the way you live.
in love. in faith.
in purity.

let them look
for a reason to dismiss you,

and find
a reason to follow.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Read the closing words aloud in the stillness: “let them look for a reason to dismiss you, and find a reason to follow.” What part of your heart feels most searched or comforted by 1 Timothy 4:12 right now?
paintings.zh_poem:
太年轻了——
准有人这样说过。

保罗没有叫他
去争辩，
也没有叫他
慢慢等老。

他说：
去作榜样。

在你的言语上，
在你的行为上，
在爱心、信心、
和清洁上。

就任凭他们
起初存心挑剔你，

最终却找着
跟随的理由。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在静默中轻声读出结尾的诗句：“就任凭他们起初存心挑剔你，最终却找着跟随的理由。”此刻，提摩太前书 4:12 最触动或最安慰你内心的是哪一部分？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “不可叫人小看你年轻，总要在言语、行为、爱心、信心、清洁上，都作信徒的榜样。”

paintings.title: the lyre on the wall
paintings.epigraph: “Don’t neglect the gift that is in you”
paintings.poem:
there were hands on your head once.
older hands,
heavy and warm,
and words said over you
you may have
half forgotten.

the gift
didn't leave
when the hands lifted.

it's still there,
like a lyre on the wall
no one has tuned
in a while.

take it down.
give yourself to it.

let people see you
getting better.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In 1 Timothy 4:14–15, grace meets us right beside the stones of the wall: how does the closing thought—“let people see you getting better”—steady your footing for the road ahead?
paintings.zh_poem:
曾有双手按在你的头上——
那是年长者的手，
厚重而温暖，
还有为你说出的预言，
你或许
已忘了一半。

当那双手挪开时，
恩赐并没有离开。

它仍在那里，
就像挂在墙上的一把琴，
只是许久
无人调弦。

把它取下来吧。
专心投入其中。

叫众人看出
你的长进来。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在提摩太前书 4:14–15 中，恩典就在石墙旁与我们相遇：结尾的深思——“叫众人看出你的长进来”——如何为你前面的道路稳住脚步？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “你不要轻忽所得的恩赐”

paintings.title: night and day
paintings.epigraph: “she who is a widow indeed and desolate, has her hope set on God, and continues in petitions and prayers night and day.”
paintings.poem:
no one left
to cook for.
no one coming home.

the house is quiet now,
and she fills it
with names.

her hope set on God,
the letter says.
night and day.

honor her, Paul wrote.
see that she
never goes without.

some of the strongest work
in any city
happens in a small room,
by one lamp,
on two old knees.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If today’s painting of “night and day” (1 Timothy 5:3–5) hung beside the door you walk out of this morning, how would its final line—“some of the strongest work in any city happens in a small room, by one lamp, on two old knees”—shape your choices?
paintings.zh_poem:
再没有谁
需要她做饭了。
也再没有谁会推门回家。

如今屋子安静下来，
她却用一个又一个名字
将屋子填满。

信上说，
她专心仰赖神，
昼夜不住地祈求。

保罗写道：要尊敬她，
看顾她，
叫她一无所缺。

在任何一座城里，
最有力的工作，
往往发生在一间小屋、
一盏孤灯旁、
一双年迈屈膝的膝盖上。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今天这幅《昼夜祈求》（提摩太前书 5:3–5）就挂在你清晨出门的门旁，它最后那句——“在任何一座城里，最有力的工作，往往发生在一间小屋、一盏孤灯旁、一双年迈屈膝的膝盖上”——会如何塑造你今天的选择？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “那独居无靠、真为寡妇的，是仰赖神，昼夜不住地祈求祷告。”

paintings.title: a little wine
paintings.epigraph: “use a little wine for your stomach’s sake and your frequent infirmities.”
paintings.poem:
in the middle of
instructions about elders,
witnesses, and warnings,

a line
only someone
who loved you
would write:

how is your stomach?
you're sick too often.
take care of yourself.

holiness
never asked you
to stop
having a body.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Every stop on the Pilgrim Walk shows how God meets us in ordinary places (1 Timothy 5:23)—where in your own home or work today does “holiness never asked you to stop having a body” ring true?
paintings.zh_poem:
在关于长老、
见证人与警戒的
重重嘱咐之间，

忽然出现一行
只有深爱你的人
才会写下的话：

你的胃口还好吗？
你太常生病了。
要好好照顾自己。

圣洁，
从来没有要求你
假装自己没有血肉之躯。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 天路同行的每一站都向我们显明，神如何在平凡之处与我们相遇（提摩太前书 5:23）——今天在你的家中或工作里，哪一处让你深感“圣洁，从来没有要求你假装自己没有血肉之躯”的真实？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “因你胃口不清，屡次患病，再不要照常喝水，可以稍微用点酒。”

paintings.title: nothing in, nothing out
paintings.epigraph: “For we brought nothing into the world, and we certainly can’t carry anything out.”
paintings.poem:
you came in
with empty hands.

you'll go out
the same way.

in between:
a table,
a coat,
the people you love.

godliness with contentment,
he says,
is great gain.

not the gain
that fills a storeroom.

the gain
of not needing one.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Take a slow breath and read the final line again: “the gain of not needing one.” How would you walk through the next hour differently if you carried that truth with you?
paintings.zh_title: 没有带什么来，也不能带什么去
paintings.zh_poem:
你来的时候，
两手空空。

你走的时候，
也必照样。

在这两者之间：
一张饭桌，
一件外衣，
和那些你所爱的人。

他说，
敬虔加上知足的心，
便是大利了。

不是那种
填满仓房的利，

而是根本无需仓房的
富足。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 深吸一口气，再读一遍最后那行诗：“而是根本无需仓房的富足。”如果你带着这份真理走入接下来的一个小时，你的脚步会有何不同？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “因为我们没有带什么到世上来，也不能带什么去。”

paintings.title: unapproachable light
paintings.epigraph: “dwelling in unapproachable light, whom no man has seen, nor can see”
paintings.poem:
every emperor
put his face on a coin.

this King
has never been seen.
cannot be seen.

he lives in a light
no one can walk into.

the only Ruler.
King of kings.
owing his crown
to no one.

and still
his light spills over the ridge
and reaches
the valley
where we are.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Think of a season when you knew the feeling of “every emperor put his face on a coin.” Looking through the lens of 1 Timothy 6:15–16, what does it mean to discover that “and still his light spills over the ridge and reaches the valley where we are”?
paintings.zh_poem:
每一个罗马皇帝
都把自己的头像铸在钱币上。

而这位君王，
人未曾看见，
也是不能看见的。

他住在无人能够步入的
强光之中。

那独一的主宰，
万王之王，
他的冠冕
不仰仗任何人。

然而，
他的光依然漫过山脊，
照进我们所在的
深谷里。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 回想一段你曾体会过“每一个罗马皇帝都把自己的头像铸在钱币上”那种世俗权势喧嚣的时光。透过提摩太前书 6:15–16 的眼光，发现“然而，他的光依然漫过山脊，照进我们所在的深谷里”对你意味着什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “住在人不能靠近的光里，是人未曾看见、也是不能看见的”

paintings.title: guard it
paintings.epigraph: “Timothy, guard that which is committed to you”
paintings.poem:
near the end
he calls him by name.

Timothy.

like a father at the door,
pressing something
into your hands:

this was given to you.
keep it.

not a treasure chest.
a trust.

don't trade it
for clever talk.

grace be with you.

and then the letter stops,
and the rest
is his to carry.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look closely at the open threshold in this painting (1 Timothy 6:20–21)—if you could leave one anxious weight beside it today, what would you set down?
paintings.zh_poem:
信快写完时，
他直呼他的名字。

提摩太啊。

像一位父亲在门口，
把一件宝贵的东西
郑重交在你手里：

这是托付给你的。
要守住它。

不是一口宝箱，
而是一份信托。

不要拿它
去换取乖巧的空谈。

愿恩惠常与你们同在。

信在此处停笔，
剩下的路，
要由他自己背负前行。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 细看这幅画中敞开的门槛（提摩太前书 6:20–21）——如果今天你可以把一件焦虑的重担放在它旁边，你会放下什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “提摩太啊，你要保守所托付你的”

paintings.title: your tears
paintings.epigraph: “remembering your tears, that I may be filled with joy”
paintings.poem:
he remembers
the tears.

not the sermons.
not the miles.

the tears,
perhaps at a goodbye
neither of them wanted.

now the older man
prays for him
night and day,
longing to see him.

some of us are remembered
for what we built.

some of us
for who wept
when we left.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Let your eyes rest on the brushwork and light around the tears God keeps in His bottle: what quiet prayer rises in you when you read, “some of us for who wept when we left”?
paintings.zh_poem:
他记起的，
是那些眼泪。

不是那些讲章，
也不是走过的里数。

而是眼泪——
或许落在一次
两人都舍不得的道别里。

如今，年长的人
昼夜为他祈求，
切切地想要见他。

我们当中有些人被记住，
是因为建造了什么；

有些人被记住，
是因为我们离开时，
曾有人为我们流泪。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 让目光停留在画中神所记念的眼泪与温暖光影：当你读到“有些人被记住，是因为我们离开时，曾有人为我们流泪”时，你心中升起怎样安静的祷告？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “记念你的眼泪，昼夜切切地想要见你，好叫我满心快乐。”

paintings.title: Lois and Eunice
paintings.epigraph: “the sincere faith that is in you, which lived first in your grandmother Lois, and your mother Eunice”
paintings.poem:
before it was his,
it lived at a table.

first in his grandmother, Lois.
then in his mother, Eunice.
then, Paul was sure of it,
in him.

no pulpit.
no title.
just a faith
with no pretending in it,

handed down
the way you hand down
a lamp,
still lit.

and a boy
was watching.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Linger with the movement in “Lois and Eunice” (2 Timothy 1:5) from “before it was his, it lived at a table” to “no title. and a boy was watching”—where do you find yourself along that arc today?
paintings.zh_poem:
在这信心成为他的以前，
它曾住在一张饭桌旁。

先是在他外祖母罗以心里，
后是在他母亲友尼基心里，
如今，保罗深信，
也在他心里。

没有讲台，
也没有头衔，
只有一份
毫无伪饰的信心，

代代相传，
就像传递一盏
依然亮着的灯。

而当年有个男孩，
正静静看着。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在《罗以和友尼基》（提摩太后书 1:5）中细细品味那份转折——从“在这信心成为他的以前，它曾住在一张饭桌旁”到“没有头衔……而当年有个男孩，正静静看着”——今天你发现自己处在这段弧线的哪个位置？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “想到你心里无伪之信，这信是先在你外祖母罗以和你母亲友尼基心里的”

paintings.title: stir it up
paintings.epigraph: “stir up the gift of God which is in you through the laying on of my hands.”
paintings.poem:
it isn't gone.
it's banked,
like a cook fire at dawn.
grey on top.
red underneath.

you don't need
a new fire.
you need to lean down
and breathe
on the one you have.

my hands were on your head,
Paul says.
I remember.

stir it up.

a gift from God
can go quiet.
it waits
for your breath.48
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Notice how “stir it up” (2 Timothy 1:6) arrives at: “it waits for your breath.48.” Who in your life is walking a hard stretch of road today and needs you to share this grace with them?
paintings.zh_poem:
火并没有熄灭。
它只是封在灰下，
像黎明时的灶火——
上面一层灰白，
底下依然通红。

你不需要
另起一炉新火。
你只需要俯下身，
向着已有的余烬
轻轻吹气。

保罗说：
我的手曾按在你头上，
我一直记得。

将它挑旺起来吧。

从神而来的恩赐
有时会归于沉寂，
它正等待着
你的气息。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 留意《如火挑旺起来》（提摩太后书 1:6）如何落脚于：“它正等待着你的气息。”今天在你的生命中，有谁正走在一程艰难的路上，需要你与他们分享这份恩典？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “为此我提醒你，使你将神借我按手所给你的恩赐，再如火挑旺起来。”

paintings.title: not fear
paintings.epigraph: “For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.”
paintings.poem:
the fear
came from somewhere.

not from him.

what he gave
was power
to stand,

love
to stay,

and a steady mind
to know
which one
this moment needs.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: What if the most important thing you remember before tonight is the quiet lesson of 2 Timothy 1:7: “what he gave was power to stand, love to stay, and a steady mind to know which one this moment needs”?
paintings.zh_poem:
那胆怯
不知从何而来，

但绝不是从他来的。

他所赐下的，
是得以站立的刚强，

得以留守的仁爱，

以及一颗清醒谨守的心，
好分辨眼下这一刻
最需要的是哪一样。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果在今晚入睡前，你最需要记住的是提摩太后书 1:7 那安静的启示：“他所赐下的，是得以站立的刚强，得以留守的仁爱，以及一颗清醒谨守的心，好分辨眼下这一刻最需要的是哪一样”——这会带给你怎样的力量？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “因为神赐给我们，不是胆怯的心，乃是刚强、仁爱、谨守的心。”

paintings.title: I know him
paintings.epigraph: “I know him whom I have believed”
paintings.poem:
he doesn't say
I know what I believe.

he says
I know him.

a chain on his wrist.
everyone in Asia
turned away.

and what he has left,
he hands over
like a traveler
leaving his bag
with someone he trusts.

he isn't worried
about the bag.

he knows
the hands.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Imagine standing inside this frame beside the loosened chain: what hurry or noise in your week begins to fade when you hear, “he isn't worried about the bag. he knows the hands”?
paintings.zh_poem:
他没有说：
我知道我所信的是什么。

他说：
我知道我所信的是谁。

手腕上锁着铁链，
凡在亚细亚的人
都离弃了他。

而他把仅存的一切
全然交托，
就像一个远行的人
把行囊留在
他所信赖的朋友手中。

他并不挂虑
那只行囊。

因为他认得
那双手。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象自己站在这幅画框里、守在锁链旁：当你听见“他并不挂虑那只行囊。因为他认得那双手”时，你这一周里的哪些匆忙与喧嚣开始渐渐消退？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “因为知道我所信的是谁”

paintings.title: not ashamed of my chain
paintings.epigraph: “he often refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain”
paintings.poem:
Onesiphorus.
a name hardly anyone
can say.

he came to Rome
and looked for Paul.
kept looking
until he found him.

it isn't easy
to find a prisoner.
it's harder
to be seen with one.

he came anyway,
and more than once
he was fresh air
in that place.

may we be
the ones
who keep looking.54
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Read the closing words aloud in the stillness: “may we be the ones who keep looking.54.” What part of your heart feels most searched or comforted by 2 Timothy 1:16–17 right now?
paintings.zh_poem:
阿尼色弗——
一个几乎没人
念得顺口的名字。

他来到罗马
寻找保罗，
一路打听，
直到找着为止。

要找一个囚犯
并不容易；
要让人看见你和囚犯在一起，
更需要勇气。

但他还是来了，
并且不止一次，
在那个阴暗的地方
带来一阵清风。

但愿我们也能成为
那样殷勤寻找的人。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在静默中轻声读出结尾的诗句：“但愿我们也能成为那样殷勤寻找的人。”此刻，提摩太后书 1:16–17 最触动或最安慰你内心的是哪一部分？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他屡次使我畅快，不以我的锁链为耻”

paintings.title: to others also
paintings.epigraph: “commit the same things to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also.”
paintings.poem:
Paul to Timothy.
Timothy to the faithful.
the faithful
to others also.

four hands
in one sentence.

nobody in that line
gets to be
the end of it.

somewhere back there,
someone handed it
to you.

look around.
whose hand
is open?
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In 2 Timothy 2:2, grace meets us right beside your own two hands: how does the closing thought—“look around. whose hand is open?”—steady your footing for the road ahead?
paintings.zh_poem:
保罗传给提摩太。
提摩太交托忠心的人。
忠心的人
再教导别人。

一句话里，
有四代人的手。

在这条传递的链条上，
没有任何人
应当成为终点。

在过去的某个地方，
曾有人把它
递到了你手里。

看看四周吧：
谁的手
正敞开着？
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在提摩太后书 2:2 中，恩典就在你自己的双手旁与我们相遇：结尾的深思——“看看四周吧：谁的手正敞开着？”——如何为你前面的道路稳住脚步？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “也要交托那忠心能教导别人的人。”

paintings.title: not chained
paintings.epigraph: “But God’s word isn’t chained.”
paintings.poem:
remember Jesus Christ,
risen from the dead.

that's what he writes
from a cell.

they could lock the door.
they could fasten the iron.

but the words
had already left the room.

in letters.
in a young man's memory.
on roads
to places
Paul would never see.

the preacher
was chained.

the word
walked out.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If today’s painting of “not chained” (2 Timothy 2:8–9) hung beside the door you walk out of this morning, how would its final line—“the preacher was chained. the word walked out”—shape your choices?
paintings.zh_poem:
你要记念耶稣基督
从死里复活——

这是他在牢房里
写下的话。

他们可以锁住牢门，
可以扣紧铁链。

但那些话语
早已走出了房间：

在书信里，
在一个年轻人的记忆里，
在通往保罗未曾见过的远方
那一条条道路上。

传道的人
被捆绑了，

主的道
却大步走了出去。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今天这幅《神的道却不被捆绑》（提摩太后书 2:8–9）就挂在你清晨出门的门旁，它最后那句——“传道的人被捆绑了，主的道却大步走了出去”——会如何塑造你今天的选择？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “然而，神的道却不被捆绑。”

paintings.title: faithful
paintings.epigraph: “If we are faithless, he remains faithful; for he can’t deny himself.”
paintings.poem:
we break.
he doesn't.

on our worst day
he is still
who he said he was.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Every stop on the Pilgrim Walk shows how God meets us in ordinary places (2 Timothy 2:11–13)—where in your own home or work today does “on our worst day he is still who he said he was” ring true?
paintings.zh_poem:
我们会失信，
他却不会。

即便在我们最糟糕的日子，
他依然是
他所应许的那一位。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 天路同行的每一站都向我们显明，神如何在平凡之处与我们相遇（提摩太后书 2:11–13）——今天在你的家中或工作里，哪一处让你深感“即便在我们最糟糕的日子，他依然是他所应许的那一位”的真实？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “我们纵然失信，他仍是可信的，因为他不能背乎自己。”

paintings.title: clay
paintings.epigraph: “he will be a vessel for honor, sanctified, and suitable for the master’s use, prepared for every good work.”
paintings.poem:
in a large house
there are cups of gold and silver,
and cups of wood and clay.

you might think
the master always reaches
for the shiny one.

he reaches
for the clean one.

you don't have to be gold.

you have to be
ready.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Take a slow breath and read the final line again: “you don't have to be gold. you have to be ready.” How would you walk through the next hour differently if you carried that truth with you?
paintings.zh_poem:
在大户人家，
有金器银器，
也有木器瓦器。

你或许以为，
主人伸手拿取的
总是那只闪亮的杯子。

其实他伸手拿的，
是那只洁净的杯子。

你不必非得是金器，

你只需要
预备好自己。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 深吸一口气，再读一遍最后那行诗：“你不必非得是金器，你只需要预备好自己。”如果你带着这份真理走入接下来的一个小时，你的脚步会有何不同？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “就必作贵重的器皿，成为圣洁，合乎主用，预备行各样的善事。”

paintings.title: from infancy
paintings.epigraph: “From infancy, you have known the holy Scriptures which are able to make you wise for salvation”
paintings.poem:
stay with what you learned,
he says,
and remember
who you learned it from.

before you could read,
you heard it.

a voice at bedtime.
the old promises
said over you
like a blanket.

breathed out by God.
breathed in
by a child.

and still wise enough
to bring you
all the way home.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Think of a season when you knew the feeling of “stay with what you learned, he says, and remember who you learned it from.” Looking through the lens of 2 Timothy 3:14–16, what does it mean to discover that “and still wise enough to bring you all the way home”?
paintings.zh_poem:
他说：
你所学习的、所确信的，
要存在心里，
也当记念你是跟谁学的。

在你还不认字的时候，
你就已经听见了。

睡前的声音，
古老的应许，
像一条温暖的毯子
覆在你身上。

由神所呼出，
被一个孩子
深深吸入。

并且至今仍有足够的智慧，
一路引领你
平安归家。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 回想一段你曾体会过“你所学习的、所确信的，要存在心里，也当记念你是跟谁学的”的时光。透过提摩太后书 3:14–16 的眼光，发现“并且至今仍有足够的智慧，一路引领你平安归家”对你意味着什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “并且知道你是从小明白圣经，这圣经能使你因信基督耶稣，有得救的智慧。”

paintings.title: fought, finished, kept
paintings.epigraph: “I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.”
paintings.poem:
he can see the end now.
already being poured out,
he writes,
like an offering.

no panic.
just three words
from a man at the end of the road:

fought.
finished.
kept.

then he looks past himself
to a crown
that isn't only his,
but for all
who have loved
his appearing.

it's the same
finish line.68
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look closely at the weight of the crown in this painting (2 Timothy 4:6–8)—if you could leave one anxious weight beside it today, what would you set down?
paintings.zh_poem:
如今他看见终点了。
他写道：
我现在被浇奠，
像献在坛上的祭物。

没有惊惶，
只有一个走到路终的人
留下的三句话：

打过了。
跑尽了。
守住了。

随后他的目光越过自己，
望向那顶冠冕——
不但赐给他，
也赐给凡爱慕主显现的人。

那是同一条
终点线。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 细看这幅画中公义冠冕的份量（提摩太后书 4:6–8）——如果今天你可以把一件焦虑的重担放在它旁边，你会放下什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “那美好的仗我已经打过了，当跑的路我已经跑尽了，所信的道我已经守住了。”

paintings.title: the cloak and the parchments
paintings.epigraph: “Bring the cloak that I left at Troas with Carpus when you come, and the books, especially the parchments.”
paintings.poem:
after the crown
and the finish line,
this:

bring my cloak.
I left it at Troas.
and the books.
especially the parchments.

Demas has gone.
only Luke is with me.
bring Mark along.

the great apostle,
near the end,
wants a warm coat,
something to read,
and his friends.

that isn't
a smaller faith.
that is a whole one.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Let your eyes rest on the brushwork and light around the torn and mended coat: what quiet prayer rises in you when you read, “that isn't a smaller faith. that is a whole one”?
paintings.zh_poem:
在谈完冠冕
与终点线之后，
他写下这几句：

把我的外衣带来，
就是我留在特罗亚的那件。
那些书也要带来，
更要紧的是那些皮卷。

底马已经走了，
独有路加在我这里。
把马可也带来。

这位伟大的使徒，
在人生的尽头，
想要一件保暖的外衣、
几卷可读的书，
还有他的朋友。

这并不是
更渺小的信心，
这是完整而真实的生命。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 让目光停留在画中围绕着外衣与皮卷的笔触与光线：当你读到“这并不是更渺小的信心，这是完整而真实的生命”时，你心中升起怎样安静的祷告？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “我在特罗亚留于加布的那件外衣，你来的时候可以带来，那些书也要带来，更要紧的是那些皮卷。”

paintings.title: the Lord stood by me
paintings.epigraph: “But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me”
paintings.poem:
at my first defense
no one came.
everyone left.

he says it plainly.
and then:
may it not be
held against them.

and then:
but the Lord
stood by me.

when the room empties,
it isn't empty.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Linger with the movement in “the Lord stood by me” (2 Timothy 4:16–17) from “at my first defense no one came” to “when the room empties, it isn't empty”—where do you find yourself along that arc today?
paintings.zh_poem:
我初次申诉的时候，
没有人前来相助，
竟都离弃我。

他平平淡淡地提起，
接着写道：
但愿这罪
不归与他们。

然后他说：
惟有主
站在我旁边。

当屋里的人都走光时，
房间其实并不空。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在《惟有主站在我旁边》（提摩太后书 4:16–17）中细细品味那份转折——从“我初次申诉的时候，没有人前来相助”到“当屋里的人都走光时，房间其实并不空”——今天你发现自己处在这段弧线的哪个位置？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “惟有主站在我旁边，加给我力量”

paintings.title: before time began
paintings.epigraph: “in hope of eternal life, which God, who can’t lie, promised before time began”
paintings.poem:
a promise
made before there was
a morning
to make it in.

by the only one
who has never lied.

everything else in this letter,
the elders,
the households,
the hard work on Crete,

rests on that.

you can build a life
on a word
that old.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Notice how “before time began” (Titus 1:1–2) arrives at: “you can build a life on a word that old.” Who in your life is walking a hard stretch of road today and needs you to share this grace with them?
paintings.zh_poem:
这是一个
在尚未有清晨之前
就已立下的应许。

出自那位
从不说谎的主。

这封信里的其余一切——
长老的设立、
家室的次序、
在革哩底的殷勤劳苦——

全都建立在这基石之上。

你尽可以把一生
建造在这样古老可靠的
一句话上。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 留意《万古之先的应许》（提多书 1:1–2）如何落脚于：“你尽可以把一生建造在这样古老可靠的一句话上。”今天在你的生命中，有谁正走在一程艰难的路上，需要你与他们分享这份恩典？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “盼望那无谎言的神在万古之先所应许的永生”

paintings.title: the one who stays
paintings.epigraph: “I left you in Crete for this reason, that you would set in order the things that were lacking”
paintings.poem:
Paul sailed on.
Titus stayed.

stayed with the unfinished work,
the half-built things,
the towns with believers
and no elders yet.

set in order,
Paul told him,
what is still lacking.

not a glamorous job.

the job
of the one
who stays.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: What if the most important thing you remember before tonight is the quiet lesson of Titus 1:5: “the job of the one who stays”?
paintings.zh_poem:
保罗扬帆前行，
提多留了下来。

留在未竟的工场里，
守着那些只建了一半的事工，
和那些已有信徒
却尚未设立长老的城邑。

保罗嘱咐他：
把那没有办完的事
都办整齐。

这不是一份光鲜的差事。

这是属于
那个留下来之人的
工夫。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果在今晚入睡前，你最需要记住的是提多书 1:5 那安静的启示：“这是属于那个留下来之人的工夫”——这会带给你怎样的勉励？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “我从前留你在革哩底，是要你将那没有办完的事都办整齐”

paintings.title: an open door
paintings.epigraph: “given to hospitality, a lover of good”
paintings.poem:
the list for leaders
isn't long on talent.

not quick-tempered.
not greedy.
not violent.

and then:
given to hospitality.

in God's house
a leader is someone
whose own door
is open,

whose table
always has room
for one more.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Imagine standing inside this frame beside the table set before you: what hurry or noise in your week begins to fade when you hear, “in God's house a leader is someone whose own door is open, whose table always has room for one more”?
paintings.zh_poem:
对教会领袖的要求，
并没有列出许多才华。

不暴躁，
不贪财，
不打人。

接着是：
乐意接待远人。

在神的家里，
作领袖的人，
是自己家门常开的人，

是饭桌上
永远能多添一副碗筷的人。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象自己站在这幅画框里、守在摆设整齐的饭桌旁：当你听见“在神的家里，作领袖的人，是自己家门常开的人，是饭桌上永远能多添一副碗筷的人”时，你这一周里的哪些匆忙与喧嚣开始渐渐消退？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “乐意接待远人，好善”

paintings.title: to the pure
paintings.epigraph: “To the pure, all things are pure”
paintings.poem:
the same field
at sunrise.

one heart sees
a thing to grab.

another sees
a thing to thank God for.

it isn't the field
that's different.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Read the closing words aloud in the stillness: “it isn't the field that's different.” What part of your heart feels most searched or comforted by Titus 1:15 right now?
paintings.zh_poem:
同一片日出时的田野。

一颗心看见的，
是可以攫取之物。

另一颗心看见的，
是可以向神感恩之物。

不同的，
从来不是那片田野。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在静默中轻声读出结尾的诗句：“不同的，从来不是那片田野。”此刻，提多书 1:15 最触动或最安慰你内心的是哪一部分？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “在洁净的人，凡物都洁净”

paintings.title: teachers of what is good
paintings.epigraph: “teachers of that which is good”
paintings.poem:
no pulpit here either.
a kitchen.
a courtyard.

the older women,
Paul says,
are teachers
of what is good.

not lecturers.
teachers,
the way one hand
shows another
how to work the dough.

how to love.
how to be kind
when the day is long.

it comes from someone
who has done it,
beside you.84
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In Titus 2:3–4, grace meets us right beside your own two hands: how does the closing thought—“it comes from someone who has done it, beside you.84”—steady your footing for the road ahead?
paintings.zh_poem:
这里也没有讲台。
只有一间厨房，
一处院落。

保罗说，
年老的妇人
要用善道教训人。

不是站在高处宣讲，
而是像一双手
教另一双手
怎样揉好面团。

怎样去爱，
怎样在漫长疲惫的日子里
依然温和恩慈。

这教导来自一个
已经在你身旁
亲身走过的人。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在提多书 2:3–4 中，恩典就在你自己的双手旁与我们相遇：结尾的深思——“这教导来自一个已经在你身旁亲身走过的人”——如何为你前面的道路稳住脚步？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “用善道教训人”

paintings.title: grace has appeared
paintings.epigraph: “For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all men”
paintings.poem:
grace didn't arrive
as an idea.

it appeared,
the way morning appears
over the edge of the sea,
all at once,
and for everyone.

and it teaches us,
the letter says.
to say no
to what ruins us.
to live
sober, upright, godly,
right here
in this present age.

grace came once.

we are watching
the horizon
for its appearing.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If today’s painting of “grace has appeared” (Titus 2:11–13) hung beside the door you walk out of this morning, how would its final line—“we are watching the horizon for its appearing”—shape your choices?
paintings.zh_poem:
恩典临到时，
并不是一个抽象的观念。

它是显明出来的——
就像清晨从海平面上
豁然升起，
一瞬间照亮全地，
临到每一个人。

信上说，
这恩典教训我们：
向那败坏我们的事说不，
在今世
自守、公义、敬虔度日。

恩典已经来过一次。

如今我们正凝望天际，
等候荣耀的显现。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今天这幅《神的恩典已经显明》（提多书 2:11–13）就挂在你清晨出门的门旁，它最后那句——“如今我们正凝望天际，等候荣耀的显现”——会如何塑造你今天的选择？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “因为神救众人的恩典已经显明出来”

paintings.title: his own
paintings.epigraph: “purify for himself a people for his own possession, zealous for good works.”
paintings.poem:
he gave himself
to buy us back.

not to make us
names on a list,

but a people
he calls
his own.

and people
who are held like that
get restless
to do good.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Every stop on the Pilgrim Walk shows how God meets us in ordinary places (Titus 2:14)—where in your own home or work today does “and people who are held like that get restless to do good” ring true?
paintings.zh_poem:
他舍了自己，
把我们赎回。

不是为了让我们
只作名册上的一个名字，

而是成为一群
他称为“自己的”子民。

而那些被如此珍爱、
如此怀抱的人，
心里总会按捺不住地
热心为善。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 天路同行的每一站都向我们显明，神如何在平凡之处与我们相遇（提多书 2:14）——今天在你的家中或工作里，哪一处让你深感“而那些被如此珍爱、如此怀抱的人，心里总会按捺不住地热心为善”的真实？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “又洁净我们，特作自己的子民，热心为善。”

paintings.title: we too
paintings.epigraph: “But when the kindness of God our Savior and his love toward mankind appeared”
paintings.poem:
we too,
Paul says.
not you.
we.

foolish once.
led around by what we wanted.
envious.
hating,
and hated.

that's who we were
when kindness
walked in.

not because of anything
we had done.
because of his mercy.

so be gentle
with the ones
still standing
where you stood.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Take a slow breath and read the final line again: “so be gentle with the ones still standing where you stood.” How would you walk through the next hour differently if you carried that truth with you?
paintings.zh_poem:
保罗说：
我们从前也是这样。
不是说“你们”，
而是“我们”。

从前也是无知，
被私欲牵着走，
怀着嫉妒，
彼此相恨，
也惹人憎恶。

当恩慈走进门来的时候，
我们原本就是那副模样。

并不是因我们自己
所行的义，
乃是照他的怜悯。

所以，要温柔地对待那些
仍站在你昔日原处的人。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 深吸一口气，再读一遍最后那行诗：“所以，要温柔地对待那些仍站在你昔日原处的人。”如果你带着这份真理走入接下来的一个小时，你的脚步会有何不同？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “但到了神我们救主的恩慈和他向人所施的慈爱显明的时候”

paintings.title: poured out richly
paintings.epigraph: “the washing of regeneration and renewing by the Holy Spirit, whom he poured out on us richly”
paintings.poem:
washed.
made new.
poured out on.

not a few drops
measured to what we deserved.

a jar
tipped
all the way over.

richly.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Think of a season when you knew the feeling of “washed. made new.” Looking through the lens of Titus 3:5–6, what does it mean to discover that “a jar tipped all the way over. richly”?
paintings.zh_poem:
洗净。
更新。
浇灌下来。

不是按我们配得的份量
吝啬地滴下几滴。

而是整只水罐
彻底倾倒。

厚厚地浇灌。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 回想一段你曾体会过“洗净。更新”的时光。透过提多书 3:5–6 的眼光，发现“而是整只水罐彻底倾倒。厚厚地浇灌”对你意味着什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “借着重生的洗和圣灵的更新。圣灵就是神借着耶稣基督我们救主厚厚浇灌在我们身上的”

paintings.title: grace be with you all
paintings.epigraph: “Grace be with you all.”
paintings.poem:
the last lines
are travel plans.

come to me at Nicopolis.
I've decided to winter there.
send Zenas and Apollos on their way,
and see that they lack nothing.

still planning.
still sending.
still making sure
the ones on the road
have what they need.

then the word
he never forgets
to end with.

grace.

to Timothy.
to Titus.
to all of you.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look closely at the quiet centerpiece of “grace be with you all” in this painting (Titus 3:12–15)—if you could leave one anxious weight beside it today, what would you set down?
paintings.zh_title: 愿恩惠常与你们众人同在
paintings.zh_poem:
全信最后几行，
是行程的安排：

你要赶紧往尼哥波立去见我，
因为我已经定意在那里过冬。
你要送西纳和亚波罗起行，
叫他们没有缺乏。

仍在筹划，
仍在差遣，
仍挂记着
叫路上的同工
得着需用的供应。

最后，是他每次停笔时
从不忘记的那个词：

恩惠。

归与提摩太，
归与提多，
也归与你们众人。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 细看这幅画中《愿恩惠常与你们众人同在》那安静的画面中心（提多书 3:12–15）——如果今天你可以把一件焦虑的重担放在它旁边，你会放下什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “愿恩惠常与你们众人同在！”

zh_subtitle: 提摩太前后书与提多书诗画集
zh_beforeYouBegin:
这是年长者写给年轻人的书信。保罗写信给在以弗所的提摩太和在革哩底的提多，谈及长老与家室、祷告与饭食，以及昼夜点着灯祈祷的寡妇。随后，在罗马的监牢里，他最后一次写信给提摩太：记念你的外祖母罗以和你的母亲友尼基，把神赐给你的恩赐再如火挑旺起来，当跑的路我已经跑尽了，并且请你在冬天以前把我的外衣和那些皮卷带来。

本书以四十首短诗走过这三卷书信，共分五部分：前两部分属提摩太前书，中间两部分属提摩太后书，最后一部分属提多书。每首诗旁配有一幅画，上方引有一句经文。画面停留在这几封信所触及的器物上——一卷书信、一炉封存的炭火、一只瓦杯、一件叠好的外衣——而将面容留给你去想象。

这些诗并非圣经本身，只是一个读经的人对经文的回应。请翻开提摩太前后书与提多书与本书一同阅读，让神真实的话语作最终的定音。
